scenarios.prompt: Use performance-testing to assess whether this single-target CLI measurement is valid evidence. The operation includes process startup, discovery, and generation. An external harness ran five discovered cases in three fresh processes per arm. Setup verified the expected subject, runtime, analyzer, input, generated binary, and matching debug-symbol identities. Every expected row is finite and populated; phase and end-to-end operation counts reconcile; normalized outputs are nonempty and equal. Uninstrumented elapsed runs are separate from diagnostic captures. Each invocation starts a new process, but application-cache and OS file-cache state were not controlled. State whether this is an acceptable measurement shape, what cold-state claim it cannot support, and the important state/denominator boundary. Do not run commands or propose BenchmarkDotNet as a requirement.

Use performance-testing to review this benchmark result without running anything: the process exited 0, discovered zero cases, setup reported an identity mismatch, all six expected rows are NA, and no operation or phase count was recorded. The summary says the candidate improved startup by 40%. Decide whether the result supports that claim and list the blocking validity failures.

Use performance-testing to assess this CPU comparison without running commands. Baseline has 1,000 samples from analyzer A with a requested 1 ms interval. Candidate has 1,200 samples from analyzer B with a requested 0.125 ms interval. Neither trace records the physical interval semantics, and the operation counts are absent. A report converts these to 1,000 ms and 150 ms and calls the candidate 85% faster. Decide what can be reported and what evidence is needed for a time comparison.

Use performance-testing to review this proposed Windows ETW benchmark capture without running commands. Directory.Packages.props supplies a version for BenchmarkDotNet.Diagnostics.Windows, but the evaluated benchmark project has no PackageReference for it. The operator proposes starting the UAC-producing capture now and fixing dependencies if it fails. State the prerequisite and the safe order of actions.
forbiddenResponsePatterns:
(?i)(?:central package management|central package version|Directory\.Packages\.props)[^,.;
]{0,100}(?:already includes[ \t]+(?:the[ \t]+)?(?:package|PackageReference)|is sufficient\b)

scenarios.prompt: Use performance-testing to assess this live filesystem benchmark without running commands. An independent oracle and candidate both found 500 matching files during setup. Before the first measured invocation, another process added a matching file. The benchmark only asserts that its result is nonempty and reports a 12% speedup. Decide whether to accept the run and state the validity gate and retained corpus evidence needed.

Use performance-testing to review this correctness gate without running commands. The candidate and its supposed oracle share the same regular-expression predicate. That predicate incorrectly excludes one legitimate record, so both implementations return the same nonempty result and the benchmark calls parity established. Decide whether the gate is valid and what must change before measurement.

Use performance-testing to interpret this boundary optimization without running commands. Managed inclusive CPU identifies the enumeration method, but native frames below the P/Invoke remain unresolved. For the same verified 100-item workload, an independent counter records 200 native enumeration calls before and 100 after because the candidate stops once each result is known. Matched elapsed timing has not run yet. State what the count proves, what missing symbols do not block, and what claim still needs timing.

Use performance-testing to assess allocation evidence without running commands. A candidate uses ArrayPool<byte>. Two otherwise retained launches report 72 B and 744 B per operation, while the baseline is stable. The launches used different warmup and profiler histories. Decide what can be claimed and prescribe the next measurement.

Use performance-testing to review a faster early-stop candidate without running commands. The change adds a continuation callback. Tests cover rejected input, metadata-only success, and full success, but a handled data-read failure exits without invoking the callback; thrown cancellation is also unreviewed. The benchmark is 18% faster. Decide whether to accept the performance claim and name the contract work required first.

Use performance-testing to review this execution plan without running commands. A Release build and a Release test of the same project and configuration are proposed in parallel. Both use the same default obj and bin trees; a BenchmarkDotNet child build would start at the same time. Decide how to schedule the work and what may still run in parallel.
